Byomkesh.description: A renowned detective known as a 'truth-seeker' who investigates crimes with keen observation, accompanied by his close friend and chronicler who narrates their stories.

Sadananda Sur.description: An elderly, secretive resident of Baghmari whose mysterious death is central to the case; his family includes his sister Sushila and her husband Prankeshta Pal, a railway line-inspector.

Amrito.description: A young, eccentric, and talkative orphan in Baghmari who is ultimately murdered; he lived with his uncle, a simple villager who hosts the investigation.

Patal.description: One of the young men from Baghmari, a friend of Amrito, who helps Byomkesh with the investigation.

Dashu.description: Another young man from Baghmari, part of Amrito's circle and involved in the events surrounding the murder.

Gopal.description: A young man from Baghmari, friend of Amrito, who participates in the investigation.

Nadu.description: A young villager who chases Amrito to defend the honor of his wife, Papia, after she is insulted and embarrassed by Amrito's antics.

Hiru.description: The elderly headman of Baghmari village, who interacts with Sadananda Sur.

Inspector Sukhamay Samanta.description: The local police inspector in Santalgola, outwardly cooperative but secretly resentful of Byomkesh.

Bhagabati-babu.description: A trader in Santalgola who once employed Amrito.

Bishwanath Mallik.description: The owner of a rice mill and illegal arms dealer revealed as a murderer, served by his loyal chief accountant Nilkantha Adhikari.

Monotosh.description: The ticket-checker at Santalgola station, quick-witted and talkative.

Haribilash-babu.description: The grave and taciturn stationmaster at Santalgola.

Rakhal Das.description: A Bengali employee at Badridas' mill, dismissed and eager to provide information against his employer.

Jamnadas Gangaram.description: A prominent local dealer who receives an anonymous letter from Byomkesh.

Nafar Kundu.description: A local warehouse owner who becomes a suspect after opium is found in his rice consignment.

Baghmari.description: A village near Santalgola, central to the story's events and the site of the murders.

Santalgola.description: A large railway station and small town near Baghmari, where much of the investigation takes place.

Calcutta.description: A major city (now Kolkata), referenced as the destination for Sadananda Sur's trip.

Kailashpur.description: The village where Nadu's wife's parents live, a few stations from Santalgola.

Ramdihi Junction.description: A railway junction where Prankeshta Pal is stationed and where Sadananda Sur's trunk is deposited.

Marwari.description: An Indian ethnic and business community, often associated with trade and commerce.

Hindustanis.description: People from the Hindi-speaking regions of northern India, referenced as part of the local population.

Gurkha.description: A member of a group of soldiers of Nepalese origin, often employed as guards.

Ayurvedic.description: Referring to Ayurveda, the traditional Indian system of medicine.

Badridas Giridharilal.description: Badridas Giridharilal is a Marwari owner of a rice mill in Santalgola, suspected due to his black horse and evasive answers.

Bishwanath Rice Mill.description: A large rice mill in Santalgola owned by Bishwanath Mallik.

Independence.description: Refers to Indian Independence in 1947, after which the country faced new challenges.

American soldiers.description: Refers to US military personnel who camped in the area during World War II.

babu.description: A respectful term for a man, often used for gentlemen or officials in Bengal.

da.description: A Bengali suffix meaning 'elder brother', used as a form of address for older males.

rest house.description: A government-run guesthouse for officials or travelers, common in India.

paddy.description: Unhusked rice, a staple crop in Bengal and much of India.

jalebis.description: A popular Indian sweet made by deep-frying batter in circular shapes and soaking in syrup.

postmortem.description: An autopsy; the medical examination of a body after death to determine the cause.

hand grenade.description: A small bomb thrown by hand, referenced as a weapon in the story.

booby trap.description: A concealed or disguised device intended to cause harm when triggered.

sari.description: A traditional Indian garment for women, consisting of a long piece of cloth draped around the body.

kurta.description: A loose, collarless shirt worn in South Asia, often by men.

shawl.description: A piece of fabric worn over the shoulders, common in Indian attire.

trolley.description: A small railway vehicle used for inspection or maintenance of tracks.
